idea-plugin.name: Code Scope
idea-plugin.description:
Draws your data structures while you debug: arrays, lists, stacks, queues, matrices, pointers, objects, trees, graphs and recursion, step by step, with a plain-language explanation of what each line changed.

Debug any Java file. The panel opens on the right when the debugger stops; step with F8 or F7. The panel and its explanations follow the system language (English or Portuguese).

Runs locally: no account, no browser, nothing sent to the internet.

Open source (MIT): github.com/celoramos/Code-Scope
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.9.2
  • New samples in Tools > Code Scope > Open a Sample: selection sort, insertion sort, matrix sum and a stack calculator.
  • Collections never show as their size in brackets: an object field holding an array shows its items (stack: [1, 2]), and a returned list shows its items instead of the debugger's internal text.
  • A Stack received as a parameter is no longer drawn upside down, and the value a method returned is part of the sentence about the call that finished.
0.9.1
  • Call stack: objects and null show in earlier calls, so a recursion over a tree shows the node of each call.
  • Stepping faster than the panel reads: it says how many steps were left out instead of comparing distant steps.
  • Enums show as the constant (Cor.VERMELHO); records and classes with their own toString show their fields.
0.9.0
  • Tools > Code Scope: Presentation Mode (larger panel and text) and Open a Sample.
  • Warns when you resume (F9) between breakpoints and steps were skipped.
  • Details button: each step as a memory change, like v[1]: 5 → 3.
  • Guided exercises and teacher notes in comments (@exercise, @expect, @note).
  • Save a GIF, save and reopen a session, compare sessions and search the history.
  • Priority queues as trees, deques, 3D arrays and objects inside matrices.
